definitions.explanation: The sovereign ruler of an empire. Used primarily for foreign emperors (Roman, Chinese, etc.) and historically for the Chinese-style title. For the Japanese emperor, 天皇 is the standard term.

examples.japanese: ローマ{皇帝|こうてい}の{歴史|れきし}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: I studied the history of the Roman emperors.

examples.japanese: ナポレオンは{自|みずか}ら{皇帝|こうてい}の{位|くらい}に{就|つ}いた。
{中国|ちゅうごく}の{歴代|れきだい}{皇帝|こうてい}は{天|てん}の{命|めい}を{受|う}けて{国|くに}を{治|おさ}めたとされる。
examples.english: The successive emperors of China were said to rule the country by the Mandate of Heaven.

notes:
CONTRAST:
{皇帝|こうてい} vs. {天皇|てんのう} — {皇帝|こうてい} is used for emperors in general (especially foreign ones), while {天皇|てんのう} refers specifically to the Emperor of Japan. Using {皇帝|こうてい} for the Japanese emperor is considered incorrect in modern Japanese.

{皇帝|こうてい} vs. {王|おう} / {国王|こくおう} — {皇帝|こうてい} (emperor) rules an empire, while {王|おう} or {国王|こくおう} (king) rules a kingdom. An emperor outranks a king in the traditional hierarchy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初代|しょだい}{皇帝|こうてい} (first emperor)
- {皇帝|こうてい}の{座|ざ} (the imperial throne)
- {皇帝|こうてい}ペンギン (emperor penguin)
